newsitem.title: INDIA: India must tap insurance to finance infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: India must tap insurance to finance infrastructure.

text.p: India needs to open its state-controlled insurance sector and access global markets to shore up its creaking infrastructure facilities, the U.S ambassador said on Thursday.

"Opening the insurance sector will help to create a substantial pool of long-term capital for investment in infrastructure and other core sectors..." ambassador Frank Wisner told a business conference in New Delhi.
India's core sector needs huge amounts of capital in the next five to ten years, Wisner said.
India needs to invest about $200 billion in infrastructure in five years to support a double-digit industry growth rate, analysts say.
Speaking at the three-day conference of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in New Delhi, Wisner said that India was highly unlikely to be able to fund all its infrastructure needs.
"In this day of global financial markets, it does not make sense, nor would it be possible, for India to finance all of this development and growth from domestic resources alone," Wisner said.
"India's policy decision in 1991 to begin to open its economy to the world gave it access to the kinds of international flows needed to supplement India's own resources," he added.
India began liberalising trade, industry and banking in 1991 as part of a sweeping programme to dismantle decades of socialist controls.
But so far the insurance sector has not been opened to private enterprise and the sector is controlled by two monoliths, the Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) and General Insurance Corporation (GIC).
Industry officials say the value of India's insurance industry is about 150 billion rupees ($4.4 bln) and the sector is growing at the rate of about 11 percent per year.
About 22 foreign firms from the U.S., Canada, Switzerland, Germany, the Middle East and Japan plan to enter the Indian insurance market, insurance sector officials say.
